title: RespawnPack machine-readable artifact registry
generatedBy: hand-authored; fenced against the code by kernel/schema.test.mjs
why: A schema nobody points at drifts from its artifact silently, and an artifact nobody declared is invisible to every review that reads this directory.

⛔ AN INVENTORY BUILT FROM WHAT IS PRESENT CANNOT REPORT AN ABSENCE. That sentence has been the finding of two separate correction rounds in this program — hooks derived from readdirSync, then kernel subsystems derived from readdirSync — so this registry is DECLARED, and the fences run in BOTH directions: every write site in the code must map to a family here, and every family here must name a schema that exists and a writer that exists.

Schemas are NORMATIVE DECLARATIONS verified in tests. The procedural loaders in kernel/lib/ remain the production validators; nothing here runs on an installed target's critical path, and no dependency was added to the zero-dependency runtime.

durabilityClasses.tracked: Committed to the project's repository. Survives a clone. The founder or their tooling may edit it.
durabilityClasses.runtime: Under .respawnpack/, gitignored, machine-local. Autonomy and session state must NEVER travel in a clone.
durabilityClasses.ci-artifact: Produced by a CI run, uploaded, and discarded. Never committed.

families.declaresSchemaVersionNote: ⛔ A REAL GAP, DECLARED. readContract() degrades anything it cannot interpret to {mode:'collaborate'}, so an unrecognised future shape fails safe rather than being mis-read. That is why it has not bitten; it is not the same as it being right.
families.readersNote: The task runner reads this document through core/_io.js's classifying boundary rather than through hooks/_runtime.js readContract, and the difference is deliberate: readContract degrades an unreadable file to `collaborate`, which is the conservative answer for a HOOK deciding how much ceremony a session owes, and the DANGEROUS one here — `collaborate` is exactly what a closed delegation looks like, so degrading would turn a read failure into 'the task was completed'. hooks/stop-savepoint.js (P5-CT-7) is the third reader in that position and takes the same route for the same reason: its delegation gate asks whether a bounded task was ever closed, and a degraded read that answered `collaborate` would report an unattested delegation as a finished one.

This archive is where a `contract complete --met` attestation actually lands: closing a delegation returns the runtime pointer to collaborate, so contract.json alone can say a delegation is no longer open and cannot say WHICH criteria were restated. The task runner therefore reads both — contract.json for openness, this for the attestation record — and treats a closed contract with no matching record here as CANNOT_DETERMINE.

families.why: the 2026-08-07 field run §4. Without a receipt, "nobody ran a savepoint" and "a savepoint ran and could not finish" are indistinguishable, so the Stop hook repeated an instruction that could not succeed once per turn for eight hours. This is the one artifact that crosses the kernel/hooks boundary in the WRITE direction — the kernel writes it, only the hook tree reads it — which is why it is a registered family rather than a marker file: two components agreeing on a shape is exactly what this registry exists to keep from drifting.

the hooks-and-install audit §6 items 4-6 and the core-adapters-ops audit §3 items 3-4. The receipt of ONE task attempt: which out-of-band gates the runner ran in its own process, whether the kernel archived a `contract complete --met` attestation for every recorded acceptance criterion, and whether the handoff for the next reader survived. It exists so that 'a task session ran' and 'the task is done' can never again be the same observation — the failure the savepoint receipt already closed one level down.
families.writerNote: ⛔ CREATED WITH open(path,'wx') AND NEVER REPLACED (anti-drift item 40), which is why the attempt number is in the FILENAME rather than the file being one fixed name rewritten by the next run the way savepoint-attempt.json is. The number is the same as the turn record it describes, so task-attempt-T-1-003.json pairs with .respawnpack/runtime/tasks/T-1/turn-003.json; a receipt path that is already taken is reported with the first record it holds, never resolved by overwriting it. First registered family whose writer lives under adapters/ — adapters/ is pack-repo-only today (install/_sources.js copies adapters/claude-code/interactive and nothing else), so this artifact appears in a TARGET only when the runner is pointed at one from a pack checkout.
families.readersNote: No reader in this tree yet. The hooks-and-install audit §6 item 5 names hooks/stop-savepoint.js and the next session as the intended consumers, and that wiring is P5-T-16c and P5-CT-7 — both of which gate on the CONTRACT rather than on this receipt, so neither needs it to do its job. Named here in prose rather than as a `readers` entry because listing a reader that does not read it would make this registry's own reader fence a check of nothing.

families.why: the class audit Class G, 'The offload path'. The receipt of ONE bounded, hookless unit of work carried to a model provider: which capability register decided the route, what the three cheap probes said about each family BEFORE anything was spent, which family and model were chosen and why, which prompt envelope composed the request, what the provider reported, and the digests of the input and the output. It exists so that 'a model answered' and 'this model, chosen for this reason, answered' can never be the same observation — the same failure the task-attempt receipt closes one layer up, applied to a choice nobody could previously audit because receipts recorded the tool list and never the model.
families.writerNote: ⛔ CREATED WITH open(path,'wx') AND NEVER REPLACED (anti-drift item 40), and the id in the FILENAME is DERIVED from the input digest and the task class rather than generated. That is deliberate: a random id would make every run a new path and the exclusive create a formality, whereas a derived one makes the same unit of work against the same project land on the same path, so a repeat is refused rather than recorded twice with two answers and no way to tell which one the operator acted on. ⛔ AND NO CREDENTIAL HAS A FIELD TO TRAVEL IN (anti-drift item 52): the schema declares no property for a prompt, a response body, a header set or an environment value, and the writer never reads `env[apiKeyEnv]` at all — the environment MAP is handed to adapters/openai-compatible/client.js, which reads the variable inside the request that needs it and scrubs its own results before they come back. Like task-attempt, this writer lives under adapters/, which install/_sources.js does not copy, so this artifact appears in a TARGET only when the offload is pointed at one from a pack checkout.
families.readersNote: No reader in this tree. The audience is the operator and a later reviewer asking which model produced a given answer and on what evidence, which is the question Class G opens with. Named in prose rather than as a `readers` entry because listing a reader that does not read it would make this registry's own reader fence a check of nothing.

excluded.reason: A hardening-program record, not a product runtime artifact. NO CODE READS IT — verified by the reader-coverage fence. It is hand- and agent-authored prose-in-JSON whose shape is deliberately free to grow as the program records new findings; schematising it would freeze an audit log.

The same class as HANDOFF.json, in markdown: the truth audits, the evidence map, the overclaim inventory and the dogfood transcripts. They are append-only records of what was found and when, read by people rather than by code, and their value comes precisely from being free to record a finding in whatever shape that finding has. A schema over an audit log would freeze the vocabulary of the next defect before it is known.

Claude Code owns this format. The installer MERGES into it and the uninstaller removes only what it placed; declaring a schema for someone else's file would invite this pack to enforce a shape it does not define. The install↔uninstall lockstep fence in install/uninstall.test.mjs is what actually protects it.
Claude Code owns this format. Only the presence of the `respawn-memory` server entry is ever read; no field of it is accessed.

Shipped SOURCE, not a generated artifact — it is the input the installer merges. Its correctness is fenced by the per-(event, matcher) tuple comparison against the installed settings.json, which is a stronger check than any schema.

npm owns these formats, publishes them, and changes them between major versions. They are also not RespawnPack state: nothing in kernel/ or hooks/ writes either file, and the only thing read from a package.json anywhere is its EXISTENCE, as the evidence that proves a Node profile to the quality gate. A schema here would document npm's decisions as if they were this pack's.
